description: A compatibility adapter that preserves Self-EvolveRec diagnostics while allowing the underlying SASRec architecture to evolve. It uses available public data and selects models by macro-average validation HR@10 across all four Amazon categories.
motivation: Keep diagnostics comparable and executable across model changes without relying on unavailable review data, hidden test labels, or unobserved simulator traits.
implementation_notes: Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device) and run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Bind view.model to the trained nn.Module and preserve or adapt item_emb, log2feats, predict_score, user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Each training batch contains (None, sequence, positive, negative), with tensors shaped B × L. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps; mark unsupported probes unavailable. Preserve all four dataset routes. Generate full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for twenty real training users, five per category. Use preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, and the pinned validation protocol; exclude test information from search.
pseudocode:
initialize DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
for each diagnostic:
    verify required data and model interfaces
    if unsupported: record unavailable with explanation
    else: compute diagnostic using public training data
for each category:
    recommend unseen items from the full catalog to five selected training users
return metrics, metric_definitions
select model using mean validation HR@10 across all four categories

originality.positive: Makes diagnostic compatibility and observable-data restrictions explicit for evolving architectures.
originality.negative: An integration specification rather than a new recommendation algorithm or learning objective.

future_potential.positive: Can support consistent diagnosis across multiple model architectures and guide subsequent experiments.
future_potential.negative: Recommendation improvements remain unproven; diagnostic findings must be validated through controlled training trials.

code_difficulty.positive: The fixed constructor, batch format, and return contract provide a clear implementation boundary.
code_difficulty.negative: Architecture changes require careful adaptation of feature extraction, scoring, and probes; full-catalog recommendation adds computational cost.
